question.text: A first-time AIF manager is stuck between using outside counsel and in-house for the fund documentation. Which combination CORRECTLY matches the role with its primary deliverable?

answer.text: Legal Counsel — NAV computation; Tax Advisor — drafting the Trust Deed.
Legal Counsel — empanelling the RTA; Tax Advisor — filing the PPM with SEBI.
Legal Counsel — drafting the Trust Deed, IMA, LPA and contribution agreements; Tax Advisor — advice on fund domicile, pre/post-tax NAV, TDS and advance tax.
Legal Counsel — performing quarterly valuation; Tax Advisor — auditing financial statements.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Chapter 7, legal advisors draft the Trust Deed, IMA, LPA and other contractual documents between the fund and its stakeholders; tax advisors opine on domiciling the funds (offshore vs onshore), compute pre and post-tax NAV, estimate advance tax and TDS, and support structuring for foreign investors. The roles are distinct and complementary. **The Trap:** Options A, B and D all swap roles — NAV is Fund-Admin/Valuer, RTA empanelment is Manager's decision, PPM filing is Merchant Banker, valuation is independent valuer, audit is statutory auditor. **Cross-Exam Context:** XXI-B (PM) uses tax advisors for client-level tax reporting; XV (RA) has no such role. XIX-C uniquely combines fund-level tax advisory with Section 115UB pass-through analysis. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Have a standing call with your tax advisor each quarter to flag new CBDT circulars. A mis-handled Section 9A (offshore fund manager safe harbour) or 115UB characterisation can create tax cascade for your LPs.
